verdict.rationale: LangGraph's checkpointer system supports 'time travel' (rewinding execution state) and human-in-the-loop review via interrupts, and LangSmith debugging gives visibility into state transitions — these cover state-level rollback and review, per [langgraph-docs-2], [langgraph-comm-4], [langgraph-gh-10]. However, there is no evidence of versioning or rollback of the automation/graph definition itself (e.g., diffing prior graph versions, approving/publishing new versions), only of runtime state checkpoints. Missing for 10: explicit graph/workflow definition versioning, a review/approval UI for automation changes, and independent confirmation that rollback works reliably in production beyond checkpoint replay.
